chunks: Sulayman ibn Khalid narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
Concerning a slave jointly owned by two men, one of whom freed his share, then the slave committed an offense involving one of the prescribed limits of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, he said:

If, when half of the slave was freed, he had been appraised so that the one who freed him would be made to pay half of his value, then half of him is free: he is to receive half the hadd of a free person and half the hadd of a slave. But if he had not been appraised, then he is a slave and is to receive the hadd of a slave.

key_terms.حَدًّا مِنْ حُدُودِ اللَّهِ: a prescribed legal punishment ordained by Allah
key_terms.حَدِّ الْحُرِّ: the prescribed punishment of a free person
key_terms.حَدِّ الْعَبْدِ: the prescribed punishment of a slave
key_terms.عَبْدٍ بَيْنَ رَجُلَيْنِ: a slave jointly owned by two men

ai.seo_question: How is the hadd punishment applied to a slave whose co-owner freed only his share?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a partially emancipated slave who becomes liable to one of the prescribed punishments of Allah. If the emancipation was legally completed through valuation and compensation, the punishment is divided according to his mixed status; otherwise, he remains treated as a slave for the purpose of the hadd.
